requirements.text: The tests run with the language's usual test runner (node:test/Vitest, pytest, cargo test) and need no network and no model.
A unit test runs scenario 05's book-page handler alone (no whole crawl) on a saved book page.
That unit test passes a category to the handler and checks the produced item, category included.
A test runs scenario 05's whole crawl, through the library's engine, replaying the responses recorded during one earlier live run (not live, not fabricated pages).
The whole-crawl test checks that the dataset holds the expected number of books.
A test of scenario 08's AI extraction runs from the Plan learned on the earlier run, or from a scripted model reply wired so the extraction really uses it.
That AI test fails if a real model is called (no real provider reachable, frozen Plan, or an assertion on model calls).
Any test that would reach the network fails, saying which address it tried (refused or missed requests surface with their URL).

programs.notes: runHandler on a page with the Poetry payload, a replay of a scenario-05 recording that asserts misses (method and URL), failed requests and 1000 committed, a frozen-Plan replay of scenario 08 that asserts zero model calls, and a scripted-model test in extract mode `model`. It adds a test that a handler with no document throws ResponseNotRecordedError naming the URL. The book page is an inline, hand-reduced stand-in, because the run could not create fixture files.

Covers all three tests correctly: misses named, 1000 books, a scripted reply with extract mode `model`, and a frozen Plan with zero model calls. It needlessly passes tier="browser" to run_handler (allowed because the Label forces no tier), so the handler tests need a cached browser where the http tier would do. The page is an inline stand-in.

Tests the handler on a saved file, the replayed crawl (misses named, 1000 books), a frozen Plan with zero model calls and a Frozen status, and a scripted reply under ExtractMode::Model. It adds a test that an unrecorded document or seed is refused and named.

The handler test on an HtmlResponse is right, and a socket/DNS guard names every address tried. But the crawl test runs Scrapy's engine on an invented in-memory site of 5 books served by a custom middleware, not on a recording or HTTP cache from a live run. Scrapy has no AI extraction, so its 'AI' tests exercise a self-written selector stub rather than scenario 08: a requirement the library cannot express.

Tests the handler on a page with the category, the replayed crawl (failed outcomes listed with their URLs, 1000 records), and a scripted reply in extract mode `model`, registered under the `vercel` provider name so that no real provider can answer. It checks failed outcomes rather than the report's misses, so a miss outside a crawl request, such as robots.txt, would not fail the test. The page is an inline stand-in.

api_misuses.member: page.extract under the default extract.mode (scripted model reply)
api_misuses.assumed: the model's reply is the extracted book as JSON, so one scripted data reply yields the record
api_misuses.doc_says: extract.mode defaults to `compiled`: the model writes each field's locators and transform once, kept in the Plan; only `model` mode has the model read the page and return the values

programs.notes: The handler test (saved file, category) and the replay test (misses named, failed 0, 1000 books) are right. The AI test sets ai.model but not extract.mode="model", so the compile step gets a data-shaped reply it cannot use and the test fails. It has no frozen-Plan alternative.

api_misuses.member: page.extract under the default extract::MODE (scripted model reply)
api_misuses.assumed: the model's reply is the extracted book as JSON, so one scripted data reply yields the record
api_misuses.doc_says: extract.mode defaults to `compiled`: the model writes each field's locators and transform once, kept in the Plan; only `model` mode has the model read the page and return the values

programs.notes: The handler and replay tests are right; the replay test names the missed URLs and counts 1000 records. The AI test leaves extract mode at its compiled default while scripting a data reply, so the compile fails. It skips the misses check if the report has no recording section.

The parse_book test on an HtmlResponse is right, and a socket guard names addresses. The 'whole crawl' test hand-loops the spider's callbacks over 4 invented pages, without Scrapy's engine or any live-run recording. The 'AI' test only compares a scripted string with the handler's output and exercises no extraction, since Scrapy has no AI extraction (not expressible in the library).
